text:
Milan seem increasingly likely to send Francesco Camarda out on loan again in January, with options including Monza and Frosinone in Serie A, but Serie B is more probable.
The striker was meant to be the bright future of the Rossoneri and Italian football when he first exploded onto the scene, but at the age of 18, he already seems to have hit a brick wall.
The product of the Milan youth academy had a loan experience with Lecce last season, though much of it was dominated by injury problems, scoring one goal with one assist in 23 games.
Now he is back at San Siro, scraping just six appearances between Serie A and the Europa League, only one of them in the starting XI.
Next step for Camarda
It is reported the decision has already been made to loan him out again in the January transfer window so that he can finally get some regular playing time.
Monza are said to be interested, although much would depend on whether or not current Serie A Capocannoniere Gustavo Varela is sold.
High-flying Frosinone are another interested party, according to Calciomercato, although here too there is strong competition from impressive Antonio Raimondo.
It seems more likely that the teenager will have to drop into Serie B to get a chance, with Pisa, Catanzaro, Benevento and Empoli expressing an interest.
